selection: 50 recent health reads curated for broad U.S. relevance; not a readership ranking or an exhaustive real-time news feed.

records.title: A student hated reading for years. Her podcast explores finding the right diagnosis
records.summary: A student describes her experience with dyslexia and finding an explanation for persistent reading difficulties, offering a family perspective on diagnosis.

records.title: AI, Tech Leaders Are Lobbying Trump Health Officials in a Government-Run Chat Room
records.summary: KFF investigates how technology companies and federal officials are shaping health-app policy, raising questions about medical-record privacy and oversight.

records.title: ChatGPT for Teens has special safeguards. A watchdog group finds most don't work
records.summary: NPR examines a watchdog assessment of teen chatbot safeguards, including concerns about responses to self-harm discussions and parental alerts.

records.title: ‘We Are Seen as Disposable’: Rural Residents Fight a Proposed Gas Pipeline
records.summary: A rural pipeline dispute illustrates concerns about environmental exposure and unequal public-health burdens in lower-income communities.

records.title: RFK Jr. touts vaccine injury initiative, worrying experts
records.summary: NPR reports on a federal vaccine-injury initiative and expert concerns. This is policy reporting, not evidence that established vaccine recommendations have changed.

records.title: Can GLP-1 drugs help people stop throwing away their money?
records.summary: Researchers plan to investigate whether GLP-1 medicines influence impulsive financial behavior. The proposed research does not establish a treatment benefit for spending problems.

records.title: Suicide is up among Black Americans. We need to talk about it.
records.summary: A panel discussion examines suicide and mental-health challenges among Black Americans, emphasizing community experiences and the importance of open conversation.

records.title: Medical Debt Is Crushing Hospital Patients in Los Angeles. Health Officials May Have a Fix.
records.summary: A Los Angeles effort to screen hospital patients for financial assistance offers a case study in preventing unaffordable medical bills.

records.title: ‘Medicare for All’ Is Back. Now Comes the Hard Part.
records.summary: KFF explores proposals for universal health coverage and the challenges of translating popular promises into legislation. Proposed changes are not current benefits.

records.title: New Maryland law requires radiologists inform patients of heart disease warning sign
records.summary: NPR discusses a Maryland notification requirement for blood-vessel calcium findings on mammograms. The state-specific rule is not a nationwide screening recommendation.

records.title: Mayo Clinic Q&A: What are the treatment options for brain metastases?
records.summary: Mayo outlines how specialists choose among surgery, radiation, medicines, and combined approaches when cancer spreads to the brain. Treatment is individualized.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Congress tried to stop surprise medical bills. It created another problem.
records.summary: CBS examines unintended consequences and disputed billing practices under the federal law intended to protect patients from surprise medical bills.

records.title: Food Aid Enrollment Tanks After SNAP Rule Changes
records.summary: KFF examines falling SNAP participation after rule changes and the implications for households that depend on food assistance.

records.title: Back or spine problems? Mayo Clinic experts explain where to start
records.summary: Mayo explains how different specialists evaluate persistent back or spine problems and why seeing a surgeon does not necessarily mean needing surgery.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Device helps people with paralysis communicate
records.summary: NIH describes a brain-computer interface tested in three people with paralysis that combined speech and gestures through a virtual avatar. This remains developing research.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Estimating cognitive impairment risk, timing
records.summary: Researchers combined blood biomarkers and genetic information to study future cognitive impairment. Risk estimates are not certain predictions of an individual’s diagnosis.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Improving lung cancer detection
records.summary: A targeted MRI contrast agent improved lung-cancer detection in mouse models. Further studies are needed before the approach can be established for patients.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Mayo Clinic Minute: Early screening and treatment advances improve prostate cancer outcomes
records.summary: An overview of prostate cancer screening discussions and advances in precisely targeted radiation. Screening decisions should account for individual risks and preferences.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Before Saying Yes to the Medical Test, Know the Risks and Benefits
records.summary: An overview of why direct-to-consumer medical tests, including full-body scans, can carry financial, physical, and emotional downsides as well as possible benefits.

records.title: Doctors Should Keep an Eye on Your Mix of Medication. If They Don’t, You Should.
records.summary: This report explains the importance of reviewing multiple medicines, particularly in older adults. Reducing prescriptions should involve a qualified clinician, not self-directed changes.

records.title: Mayo Clinic Q&A: What are 5 ovarian cancer signs women may overlook?
records.summary: A discussion of vague or easily overlooked ovarian cancer symptoms and why persistent changes deserve a medical evaluation rather than self-diagnosis.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Alan Alda on fighting Parkinson's with laughter
records.summary: Actor Alan Alda discusses living with Parkinson’s disease and maintaining humor and identity alongside a chronic neurological condition.

records.title: Letting go: Why holding onto grudges can be damaging
records.summary: CBS explores research and expert perspectives on resentment, stress, and forgiveness. The report discusses associations rather than promising a medical cure.

records.title: Midterms Have Revived Universal Healthcare Debate. These States Are Ahead of Everyone.
records.summary: KFF examines state efforts toward broader health coverage as the national debate returns. State proposals and political campaigns are distinct from enacted coverage.

records.title: Patient Dies by Suicide After ‘Insurance Issue’ Delayed Medicine for Lung Disease Flare-Ups
records.summary: A family’s experience with delayed COPD medication highlights questions about insurance barriers and timely access to care. The report includes discussion of suicide.

records.title: Mayo Clinic Q&A: How are rotator cuff tears treated?
records.summary: Mayo explains how clinicians assess rotator cuff injuries and choose treatment approaches, including factors affecting surgery decisions and recovery.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: People who walk more or walk faster live longer, study finds
records.summary: Harvard reviews research associating walking pace and daily steps with longevity. Observational associations do not prove that a particular walking target guarantees a longer life.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Hospitals Have a Little-Known Tool To Prevent Medical Debt. Here’s How It Works.
records.summary: This explainer examines hospital financial-assistance programs and efforts to identify eligible patients automatically, while noting that procedures differ across hospitals and states.

records.title: For sleep apnea, a dental device may be as effective as CPAP
records.summary: A small study compared dental appliances and CPAP on blood pressure and sleepiness. The article notes that CPAP remains preferred for many people with moderate or severe sleep apnea.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Rural MAHA Followers Say Trump Health Policies Haven’t Reached Their Communities
records.summary: A rural voter survey explores whether national health-policy initiatives are reaching local communities and meeting residents’ healthcare needs.

records.title: Drugs Are Widely Used To Sedate Dementia Patients. Her Sons Wanted To Keep Her Off Them.
records.summary: A family’s experience highlights difficult decisions about sedating medicines in dementia care, including treatment goals, autonomy, and caregiving responsibilities.

records.title: These 100 Nursing Homes Face Perilous Flood Risk. Minnesota Shows What Can Happen.
records.summary: KFF examines nursing homes vulnerable to flooding and the challenges of evacuating older residents, using a Minnesota incident as an example.

records.title: US Poised To Boot Legal Immigrants From Medicaid, Including Refugees and Sex-Trafficking Victims
records.summary: A report examines Medicaid eligibility changes affecting certain legally present immigrants and projected losses of coverage. Eligibility depends on specific rules and circumstances.

records.title: Confusion and Angst Follow State’s Early Rollout of Medicaid Work Rules
records.summary: Montana’s early implementation of Medicaid work requirements illustrates confusion over coverage rules. Requirements and exemptions vary, so consult official state guidance.

records.title: She Left After Waiting Hours in the Emergency Room. The ER Billed Her Anyway.
records.summary: A patient billed after leaving an emergency-room waiting area illustrates questions about facility charges and how patients can understand disputed bills.

records.title: Antiviral drug did not improve Long COVID symptoms
records.summary: NIH summarizes a clinical trial in which an extended antiviral treatment did not improve Long COVID symptoms. The finding concerns the studied regimen, not every possible treatment.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Food Safety Finds a Place Among ‘Kitchen-Table’ Political Issues
records.summary: Reporting examines how foodborne outbreaks and recalls have brought food safety into broader public discussions about everyday health protections.

records.title: Republicans and Democrats Find a Unifying Target: Pharmacy Benefit Managers
records.summary: KFF explores scrutiny of pharmacy benefit managers and state and federal proposals addressing their role in prescription pricing and pharmacy ownership.

records.title: Abortion Is on the Ballot Again as Post-Roe Policies Continue To Evolve
records.summary: KFF explains upcoming state abortion-related ballot measures and their place in the changing reproductive-health policy landscape. Rules remain jurisdiction-specific.

records.title: Carb cycling: What is it, and does it work?
records.summary: An explanation of alternating carbohydrate intake with activity levels, including why it may offer little advantage over a balanced diet for everyday exercisers.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Melatonin or magnesium: Can either supplement help you sleep?
records.summary: A review of popular sleep supplements, the strength of their evidence, and why side effects and interactions deserve attention before use.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Salmonella, E. coli, Cyclospora, and other germs that cause food poisoning: What you need to know
records.summary: Harvard explains common causes of foodborne illness, prevention, and how to find official recall and outbreak information.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Understanding orthorexia: Have your healthy eating goals gone too far?
records.summary: An overview of when a preoccupation with eating healthfully can become restrictive or disruptive, with context for recognizing concerning patterns.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Nursing Home Beds Are Becoming More Scarce
records.summary: An examination of declining nursing-home capacity considers how an aging population may affect families searching for long-term care.

records.title: Clues to what causes multiple sclerosis
records.summary: An NIH research overview examines emerging clues about multiple sclerosis and approaches to reducing disease activity. Research advances do not yet amount to a cure.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: As Health Insurance Costs Soar, Healthcare Workers Also Feel the Pinch
records.summary: Healthcare workers describe difficult coverage decisions as insurance premiums rise, illustrating affordability pressures that extend beyond any single profession.

records.title: Insurance Coverage Lags as Cancer Science, Treatment Move Forward
records.summary: New approaches to classifying cancers by genetic changes can outpace insurance coverage, creating questions about access to specialized treatment.

records.title: Porsha Williams reveals health emergency: "It all happened so fast"
records.summary: A television personality describes emergency treatment after uterine fibroids were discovered. The personal account is not a diagnostic checklist or a typical outcome for every patient.

records.title: Shingrix shingles vaccine linked with lower heart disease risks
records.summary: Harvard discusses a study linking shingles vaccination with cardiovascular outcomes. The findings should not be treated as proof of a new heart-disease indication.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed

records.title: Depression may stall development of new neurons
records.summary: NIH explains research on depression and the development of neurons in a brain region involved in memory. Mechanistic findings are not a new clinical treatment recommendation.
records.dateEvidence: Publisher displayed article date or official dated edition/feed
